To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IFNg and its receptor STAT1 function as extrinsic tumor suppressors by promoting natural immune surveillance against cancer.

IFNg/STAT 1 functions as an extrinsic tumor-suppressor system that is essential for natural tumor suppression and that the IFNg receptor/STAT1 signaling pathway is required for the induction of the innate and adaptive immune responses that are necessary for the natural suppression of cancer.

IFNg and its receptor STAT1 function as the basis of a natural tumor suppressor system and that this tumor suppressor system is responsible for the elimination of the majority of tumors that develop in mice and humans.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidating the mechanisms by which the IFNg/ STAT1 signaling pathway promotes the development of natural host responses that suppress the development of cancer.
understanding the mechanisms by which IFNg and its downstream signaling pathway involving the JAK1/STAT1 complex contribute to natural host responses against tumors.
the contributions of the IFNg/ STAT1 signaling pathway to natural host responses against spontaneous cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

IFNg and the JAK STAT pathway play a critical role as the basis of a natural host defense mechanism that functions as an extrinsic tumor surveillance system to prevent the development of cancer and to promote its regression.
IFNg and STAT1 are the extrinsic tumor suppressors that are responsible for the natural host response to cancer and for the phenomenon of cancer immunosuppression.

the IFNg receptor STAT1 signaling pathway is a tumor suppressor and that the IFNg STAT1 system functions as the basis for a natural tumor suppressor system, which we term Cancer Immunoediting, and that this system can be manipulated to promote cancer immunosurvelliance and immunotherapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the IFNg receptor STAT1 signaling pathway is a critical component of the innate and adaptive arms of host immune defenses against cancer.
STAT1 is a key component of an extrinsic immune surveillance system that is capable of detecting and destroying nascent cancer cells.
IFNg STAT1 signaling and lymphocytes function as an extrinsic tumor surveillance system to promote natural host defenses against cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the IFNg STAT1 pathway is an important component of an extrinsic immune system that functions as the basis for a tumor suppressor system and is the primary mechanism by which the host responds to cancer.

the extrinsic tumor suppressive effects of IFNg and its receptor STAT1 can be viewed as an integral part of the natural host response to cancer and that these extrinsic tumor suppressors function as the basis of a new concept of immunosuppression we term cancer immunoediting.
IFNg/STAT-1 is a key component of the innate immune system that functions as an extrinsic tumor-suppressor pathway to eliminate cancerous cells in the early phases of carcinogenesis.
